<prefix>_batch.description: Edit a document in <Kit> through its object model: one model/batch of `ops`, run in order as one undoable step (nothing changes when an op fails: a `command` op among other ops is taken back when a later op fails, and refused before anything runs where only undo could take it back, a file open in its editor or with unsaved edits; run commands with <prefix>_run then), then `load` reads objects back. Ops: create {type, fields?, ref?: "$name", in?: "<target>.<field>", at?, parent?}, set {target, field, value}, delete {target}, text.insert {target, field, index, text}, text.delete {target, field, index, count}, text.set {target, field, text}, text.mark/text.unmark {target, field, start, end, key, value?}, list.insert {target, field, item, index?}, list.move {target, field, from, to}, list.remove {target, field, index}, map.set/map.delete {target, field, key, value?}, tree.insert/tree.move {target, field, item, parent?}, command {id, params?}. A target is `root`, an object id from <prefix>_query, or a `$name` bound by an earlier create. Saves the file unless `save` is false; with `draft`, edits your draft instead (never saved). Failures answer `error.code` and the op's `index`. The answer says what the call changed (`changes`: created, changed with each field before and after, moved, deleted, by the ids the inspect and query tools use; `revision`), so there is no need to inspect again just to see that, and which diagnostics it introduced or resolved (`diagnostics: { new, resolved }`); `changesUnavailable` says why when it cannot. Pass the latest `revision` you were given for the file as `basis`: the answer then lists what others changed since (`others`), and a `conflict` (nothing ran) means others deleted, moved or changed what this call acts on: look at `others` and `conflicts`, decide again, and pass the `revision` the refusal gives. Low level: `text.set` here replaces the text together with its formatting, and created objects get default styles; for ordinary edits prefer the kit's commands (its commands and run tools), which keep formatting.

<prefix>_inspect.description: Open a document (<formats>) in <Kit> and report the document. With `preview: true` it also attaches a rendered preview to the next turn, for when you need to see it (layout, overlaps, colours); without it, it answers JSON only. With `target` (for example {"slide": 3}) it looks at only that part and lists its objects (ids, kinds, names, boxes, text, fills), which is the usual way to find what to edit; with `preview`, `target` is also the view drawn (for a timeline {"time": 3}), and `preview` in the answer says what the picture shows (its size and scale, a timeline's frames and their times). Use it before and after editing. It answers `revision`: pass it as `basis` to your next call on the file.

target.description: Look at one part: {"slide": 3} or {"page": 2} (counted from 1), or {"slideId": 260} or {"pageId": 7} (the part's `id` as inspect lists it, which stays the same when parts are added, deleted or moved), lists its objects (and previews it with `preview: true`); a diagnostic's `target` from the check tool (for example {"path": "layer:12"}) previews what it is about; {"range": "A1:J20", "sheet": "name"} lists those cells of a spreadsheet; {"paragraphs": [0, 30]} lists those paragraphs of a document (counted from 0). With `preview`, it is the view the picture shows, passed whole to a kit's own render command (`agent.render`): for a timeline {"time": 3} (seconds) for one frame or {"range": [0, 4], "frames": 6} for a contact sheet, with the kit's part, for example {"sequence": 2} or {"comp": 3}. A kit's render command takes the members its parameter schema lists (the commands tool shows it); any other is `invalid-params`, naming those it takes. renumbered.description: One line naming the ids another program renumbered in the file: each may now name another object, and what changed in them is not known. A write on one is refused (`unknown`) until an inspect gives the ids as they are now.

truncated.description: The lists were cut to 50 objects in all: how many of each were left out. Pass `changes: "all"` for every one.

unknown.description: Some of it cannot be told object by object (a kit without an object model, a document read again with unsaved edits).

unnamed.description: Changes, made in the file by another program, of objects no tool id names (a layout, shared media), counted by type and list: `{ "Media": { "changed": 1 } }`.

revision.description: The document's state this answer describes, a short opaque token: pass it as `basis` to your next call on the file. Left out of a write of a kit without an object model.

schema.description: With `describe`: the object types as JSON Schema.

<prefix>_run.description: Edit a document in <Kit> by running commands in order, then save the file. Each step is one undoable command with a JSON object of params, as documented by <prefix>_commands; `on` names the objects a step acts on by the ids <prefix>_inspect lists, and `at` where it acts (a part, a time). The kit's selection and current part are set for each step and put back after the call, so a call leaves no state behind. Stops at the first failing step and rolls the run back: the file and the document are as they were before the call, and nothing is saved. Answers each step's result and a short document summary. The answer says what the call changed (`changes`: created, changed with each field before and after, moved, deleted, by the ids the inspect and query tools use; `revision`), so there is no need to inspect again just to see that, and which diagnostics it introduced or resolved (`diagnostics: { new, resolved }`); `changesUnavailable` says why when it cannot. Pass the latest `revision` you were given for the file as `basis`: the answer then lists what others changed since (`others`), and a `conflict` (nothing ran) means others deleted, moved or changed what this call acts on: look at `others` and `conflicts`, decide again, and pass the `revision` the refusal gives. With `draft`, the steps edit your draft of the file instead (never saved); call <prefix>_draft_ready when it is done.

basis.description: The `revision` of the last answer you were given for this file. The answer then says what others (other agents, edits to the file) changed since (`others`); a write whose objects or part they deleted, moved or changed is refused with `conflict` and runs nothing.

changes.description: What the answer's `changes` lists: true (the default) the objects the call created, changed, moved and deleted, at most 50 with `truncated` counting the rest; "all" every one; false leaves `changes` out.

check.description: Check the document before and after the call and answer `diagnostics: { new, resolved }`. Defaults to true; false skips both checks.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.

preview.description: Attach a rendered preview of the document after the steps: the whole document, or `view`. Defaults to false.

save.description: Save the file after the steps. Defaults to true; a draft is never saved.

at.description: Where the step acts, for this step only: `part` as in `target` (it overrides the run's `target`), `time` in seconds for kits with a timeline.

command.description: A command id from <prefix>_commands, for example `<command>`.

on.description: The objects the step acts on, by the ids <prefix>_inspect lists. They go into the command's id parameter (its `targets` in <prefix>_commands with `detail`; do not give that parameter too), or are selected for a command that acts on the selection (`reads` lists `selection`); the selection is put back afterwards. A command that takes neither refuses `on`.

target.description: The part the steps act on, as in the inspect tool's target: {"slideId": 260} (the slide's `id` as inspect lists it; it names the same slide after slides are added, deleted or moved) or {"slide": 3} (counted from 1; whatever slide is third then). The ids the inspect tool listed for that part work in the steps; a step's `at.part` overrides it for that step. The kit's current part is as it was after the call.

view.description: What the preview shows, for a kit with its own render command (`agent.render`): a view as the inspect tool's `target` names it, for example {"time": 3} or {"slide": 2}. It is checked before any step runs; `preview` in the answer says what the picture shows. Not for drafts.

changes.description: What the call changed, objects named by the ids the inspect and query tools use (tool ids where the kit declares them), each list ordered by id. A value is given as it is, except a text over 80 characters (`{ excerpt, length }`) and a blob after value (`{ size }`); blob before values keep `{ hash, mime, size, name? }`. A list or tree field's change is told by `moved`, `created` and `deleted`. `null` when the kit cannot say (`changesUnavailable` says why); left out with `changes: false`.

edits.description: Each changed field but list and tree fields. Before and after values are optional when unavailable or intentionally omitted, including large derived values; an omitted value is not null.

id.description: A tool id; a whole number for a kit whose tool ids are numbers (as its commands take them).

parent.description: The object whose list or tree holds it (in a tree, the parent node's object, or the tree's owner for a root node); a number for a kit whose tool ids are whole numbers.

id.description: A tool id; a whole number for a kit whose tool ids are numbers (as its commands take them).

values.description: Each of them but list and tree fields, by name.

deleted.description: Objects removed, each with `at`, where a list or tree held it before.

parent.description: The object whose list or tree holds it (in a tree, the parent node's object, or the tree's owner for a root node); a number for a kit whose tool ids are whole numbers.

id.description: A tool id; a whole number for a kit whose tool ids are numbers (as its commands take them).

footprint.description: A shift of many objects stated once: the `count` objects of `parent`'s list `field` from index `from` (as the list is after the change) had only `shift.field` changed, each by `shift.by`; or the objects `ids` had only `edits` changed, each field by its `by`. They are in no other list. Pass `changes: "all"` to have each listed.

from.description: The first object's index in the list, after the change.

ids.description: Objects stated by their ids: each had only `edits` changed, each field by its `by`.

items.description: A tool id; a whole number for a kit whose tool ids are numbers (as its commands take them).

by.description: after - before; a string for whole numbers written as strings.

moved.description: Objects whose place in a list or tree changed (also in `changed` when their fields did).

parent.description: The object whose list or tree holds it (in a tree, the parent node's object, or the tree's owner for a root node); a number for a kit whose tool ids are whole numbers.

changesUnavailable.description: Why `changes` is null: the kit has no object model, the document was replaced while the call ran, or the file is open in its editor.

closed.description: A successful terminal close; no document view, save, restore or preview follows it.

completed.description: The steps that ran, in order. On failure it is empty: a run is atomic (KHP A53), and the steps before the failing one are in `rolledBack`; only when they could not be rolled back are they here. `changed` is there only when false (the step changed nothing), `result` only when the command answered one.

truncated.description: The result was cut to fit: `shown` of `total` items (of `field` when the result is an object).

conflicts.description: With `error.code` `conflict`: what others changed of what the write acts on. Nothing ran.

id.description: The object or part (`slide:3`; a whole number for a kit whose tool ids are numbers); absent when the whole document is concerned.

now.description: Where it is now: `{ parent, field, index }` (and `spelled`, its place in the command's index spelling, `"#2"`, for a step that named it so) and the fields its kit marks as its position (`start`; one named `parent`, `field` or `index` in `fields`), or a part as `{ "slide": n }`.

place.description: For a step that names what it acts on by a place: that place as the step named it (`time`, `part`, the place parameters) and `under`, the objects it names now (`unknown` when the kit cannot say).

reason.description: `deleted`; `relocated` (moved, its index, position fields or part number shifted, or for a step that names its objects by a place, under that place now or there at `basis` and moved by others); `changed` (a field the write replaces, any field of a command's target, or another agent's step at the top of the agents' undo history); `unknown` (inspect again).

diagnostics.description: The kit's check before and after the call, matched by `code` and `target`: what the call introduced and what it resolved. Left out with `check: false` or when the kit does not check documents.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

guardUnavailable.description: The call gave `basis`, but the file is open in its editor, where this server does not journal changes: why nothing was checked.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

notRun.description: Remaining steps after a terminal close.

others.description: What others changed since the call's `basis` (other agents, edits to the file made outside this server), merged into one change set by the ids the tools use, at most 50 objects with `truncated`; left out when nothing.

by.description: Who: each other agent's name on this server, `outside` for edits to the file.

edits.description: Each changed field but list and tree fields. Before and after values are optional when unavailable or intentionally omitted, including large derived values; an omitted value is not null.

preview.description: What the attached preview shows, as the kit's render command (`agent.render`) answered it beside the image: `width`, `height` and `scale`, and the kit's own members, for a timeline `sequence`, `frames` ([{time, frame, label}], the times the picture shows), `columns` and `rows`. Only for kits with a render command.

previewError.description: The preview could not be drawn; the run went as `completed` says.

revision.description: The document's state this answer describes, a short opaque token: pass it as `basis` to your next call on the file. Left out of a write of a kit without an object model.

rolledBack.description: On failure: the steps that ran before the failing one and were undone, so the document is as it was before the call and nothing was saved (KHP A53).
